Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.

Let $\star$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-involution of $U_q^-$ fixing each generator $F_i$, so that for a word $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$ one has $(F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r})^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, and let $B$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then $\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution of the Serre quotient, reverses negative words, preserves the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], commutes with the bar involution $\psi$, and preserves $B$: $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$. Consequently $\star$ preserves the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], the integral residue lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-=U_A^-\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ of [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]. On the integral crystal residue the induced map permutes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. Only this signed lattice preservation is asserted, not an unsigned $\star$-crystal theorem; the sign is what the gluing of the string-ideal global lifts requires.

Let $i\in I$ and let $e_i'$ be the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with string decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$, $u_l\in\ker e_i'$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

(i) If $u\in U_A^-$ then all $u_l$ lie in $U_A^-$. The integral projector is
$$P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l,\qquad u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu,$$
where all powers of $e_i'$ are ordinary powers, not divided by $[l]_i!$.

(ii) Define
$$I_{(i,n)}^A:=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}\bigl(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,$$
$$J_{(i,n)}^A:=\pi_\lambda\bigl(I_{(i,n)}^A\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda),$$
with $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ as in [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]. The latter is an $A$-submodule inside the field string-image subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, not a $U_q$-submodule or a $U_A$-stable lattice in general; its equality with $V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed here.

(iii) The integral residue of $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the corresponding rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is a conclusion of the subsequent string-ideal induction, not an input.

(iv) On every $U_A$-stable integrable module lattice $M_A$, if a label $\mu$ satisfies $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=-n\le-1$, then every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ satisfies the finite identity
$$u=\sum_{k\ge n}(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_iF_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u,$$
and consequently $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$. This is the exact boundary generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

Fix a root degree $\alpha$ of height $r$. Assume integral balancedness and global lifts in every degree of height $<r$ for both the negative half and all dominant highest modules, including based-quotient compatibility there and the negative-half string-ideal membership of each lower lift $G_\infty(b)$ whenever $b\in\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$. Then for every $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$:

(i) the image string ideal $J_{(i,n)}^A$ in each highest module $V(\lambda)$, with its rational zero- and infinity-chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree $\lambda-\alpha$, and its balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection maps isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\lambda\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\lambda$ in that degree;

(ii) the half ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, with balanced intersection mapping isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\infty\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$; and

(iii) their Laurent extensions are free $A$-modules with the adapted global lifts.

Freeness, the chart intersections and the eventual module saturation $J_{(i,n)}^A=V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ are conclusions, not hypotheses.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$, $V(\mu)$, $V(\lambda+\mu)$ be the simple integrable highest weight modules with highest weight vectors $v_\lambda,v_\mu,v_{\lambda+\mu}$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equip $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$ with the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure given by the coproduct $\Delta$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

(i) $v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\lambda+\mu$, and its cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)$ is isomorphic to $V(\lambda+\mu)$.

(ii) There are unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps
$$\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda+\mu)\to V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu),\qquad \Psi_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\to V(\lambda+\mu)$$
with $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(v_{\lambda+\mu})=v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ and $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)=v_{\lambda+\mu}$; they satisfy $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}\circ\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}=\operatorname{id}_{V(\lambda+\mu)}$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is injective with image $U_q(\mathfrak g)(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is surjective, and $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)=\operatorname{Im}\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}\oplus\ker\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$.

(iii) Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the contravariant form on $V(\lambda)$ of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] and similarly on $V(\mu)$; define the symmetric bilinear form on $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$ by $(u_1\otimes u_2,v_1\otimes v_2)=(u_1,v_1)(u_2,v_2)$. Then for all $u,v$ and all $i\in I$, $h\in P^\vee$,
$$(K_hu,v)=(u,K_hv),\qquad (E_iu,v)=(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad (F_iu,v)=(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$
and the maps of (ii) are adjoint: $(\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}u,v)=(u,\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}v)$ for all $u\in V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$, $v\in V(\lambda+\mu)$. In particular $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is an isometry onto its image.

(iv) The linear map $S_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\to V(\lambda)$ defined by
$$S_{\lambda,\mu}(u\otimes v_\mu)=u\quad(u\in V(\lambda)),\qquad S_{\lambda,\mu}\Bigl(V(\lambda)\otimes\sum_{i\in I}F_iV(\mu)\Bigr)=0$$
is well defined, because $V(\mu)=\mathbb Q(q)v_\mu\oplus\sum_{i\in I}F_iV(\mu)$; it is $U_q^-$-linear for the left multiplication action of $U_q^-$, and $S_{\lambda,\mu}\circ\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the unique $U_q^-$-linear surjection $V(\lambda+\mu)\to V(\lambda)$ with $v_{\lambda+\mu}\mapsto v_\lambda$. No choice principle is used.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up
to internal shift. Set $c_i(S)=\epsilon_i^L(S)$ and
$J_i(S)=\max\{n\ge0:c_i(f_i^nS)=c_i(S)\}$. This maximum is finite and
$J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for
$\beta=\operatorname{wt}(S)$. For $i\ne j$ one has $c_i(f_jS)=c_i(S)$; for
$j=i$ it stays constant or increases by $1$, and increase is equivalent to
$f_iS=f_i^LS$ and to simplicity of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L(i))$. Once it
increases, it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Put
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,
\operatorname{wt}\rangle$. The maps
$\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ are strict injective
elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at
some $i$. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic $f_i$
nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$ the actual
surviving lowering length is
$\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. All containing-weight
arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum,
leaving $R,A,D,Q$ unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the
original $P$ is added. Linear divided restriction/$G_0$ operators satisfy the
quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to
satisfy a linear Serre identity.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the comultiplication's $E_i,F_i$ formulas are
unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.

derivations.claim: Right strings and the component decomposition. Define the right string operators by $*$-conjugating the left normalized Kashiwara operators; since $*$ is an isometry of the crystal lattice and the signed crystal set, every positive crystal residue $b$ lies in exactly one right-string position $c_i(b)\ge0$. If $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}v_n$ is a lattice element with $v_n\in\ker(*e_i'*)$ and $T_n=\tilde e_i^nu$, then $v_n=T_n-\tilde f_iT_{n+1}$ lies in the lattice; induction on the largest nonzero position, using the residue partial inverse, shows a basis residue has exactly one nonzero component and that its top residue is positive. Root height makes the tails finite, so this half-version is proved directly and does not apply an integrable-module-only statement to $U^-$; conjugating through the signed lattice theorem gives the asserted signed right version, without assuming unsigned $*$.

Strict elementary embeddings. Combining the component decomposition of step 1.1 with the top-residue computation: for a positive crystal residue $b$ with $c_i(b)=0$ the string position is $0$ and the top component is $b$ itself; for general $b$ the top component is $\bar b=(e_i^*)^{c_i(b)}b$ with $c_i(\bar b)=0$ and $\epsilon_i(*b)=c_i(b)$. Hence $\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c_i(b))$ is a strict elementary embedding, every nonvacuum vertex has positive extraction at some color (otherwise all $\epsilon_i(*b)=0$ forces $b$ to be the vacuum), and the negative-half reversal $*$ permutes $B(\infty)$ without signs, the unsigned conclusion following from the signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues rather than being assumed.

Survivors of the highest-weight projection. The projection $\pi_\lambda$ kills exactly the negative-half crystal vertices with $c_i(b)>\lambda_i$ for some $i$: the string ideal decomposition of [F1] identifies the relevant ideal with the direct sum of right-string positions $n\ge\lambda_i+1$, and the crystal-lattice comparison of [F2] makes the projection commute with the crystal operators modulo $q$. The survivors therefore carry weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$ with inherited raising and surviving lowering operators and the induced $\epsilon/\varphi$; the grand-loop and tensor-product theorems of [F2] identify the resulting crystal with $B(\lambda)$.

Uniqueness by lowering words. Let $C,C'$ be two lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex. Match their vacuums and extend along lowering words: strictness of the elementary extractions makes each one-step extension unique, and the positive-extraction hypothesis ensures every nonvacuum vertex is reached by a finite lowering word. The comparison runs over finite color cycles and terminates after the height bound forced by the vertex's weight, so the isomorphism is well defined, unique and independent of the chosen lowering words.

The categorified graph. For any field and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ satisfying the hypotheses of the two one-step lemmas of [F3], the shift-orbit simple-module graph is lowering-generated with strict elementary extractions by [F3]; step 3.2 identifies it canonically with $B(\infty)$. In a first-strand cyclotomic quotient the surviving simple graph is exactly the survivor set of step 3.1, hence is $B(\lambda)$; the graph labeled by indecomposable projective covers $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled cover--simple pairing of the cover-descent lemma, since the pairing matches each cover label with its simple head without rescaling. Operators on cover labels are transported from the simple graph; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification and no general global-basis theorem is used.

Choice bookkeeping. The argument is a chain of the inherited suppliers [F1] and [F2]; the Axiom of Choice is inherited exactly through the grand-loop crystal-basis and highest-weight projection contracts used in step 3.1 (partial inverses and survivor bijections), and through no other step. No further infinite choice is made in steps 1.1, 2.1 and 4.1, which are finite string, height and word computations.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field $k$, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative $S_b$ self-dual for $D(M)_d=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_{-d},k)$ with action $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. Its projective cover $P_b$, normalized by $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P_b,S_b)=k$, satisfies $P_b^\#=P_b$ for $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,R)^\psi$. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0$ and $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S_b=L(i^r)\boxtimes S_a$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0$, normalized as above, then
$$[P_{i,r}][P_a]=[P_b]+\sum_{\epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r}m_c(q)[P_c],$$
with $m_c\in\mathbb{N}[q,q^{-1}]$ each invariant under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$. Under $\gamma$ the integral LEFT divided-string ideal $I_{(i,\ge n)}=\sum_{r\ge n}F_i^{(r)}U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of $[P_b]$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)\ge n$. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient $1$ identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

derivations.claim: Base change of projectives and covers. A finite graded projective $P$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $A$, so $B\otimes_AP$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $B$: it is finite graded projective. The quotient adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,B\otimes_AP')=\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_AP,B\otimes_AP')$, and every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes_AP$ lifts through the canonical map $P\to B\otimes_AP$; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so the induced map $\operatorname{End}^0_A(P)\to\operatorname{End}^0_B(B\otimes_AP)$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. If $P$ is indecomposable, its finite-dimensional local degree-zero endomorphism ring has no nontrivial idempotent, so a nonzero quotient has none either: $B\otimes_AP$ is zero or indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover map factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential (a submodule of $B\otimes_AP$ mapping onto $S$ pulls back to a submodule of $P$ mapping onto $S$; essentiality of the old cover makes it all of $P$), so $B\otimes_AP$ is the projective cover of $S$ with the same head. If $JS\ne0$ and $B\otimes_AP\ne0$, finite dimension [F3] supplies a simple quotient, which must be the unique head $S$; but $J$ annihilates no nonzero quotient mapping onto $S$ with $JS=0$? Precisely, the unique simple head $S$ satisfies $JS=0$, contradicting the assumption, so $B\otimes_AP=0$.

Every $B$-orbit arises and heads do not merge. Every simple $B$-module is a simple $A$-module by inflation, and its descended cover $B\otimes_AP(S)$ is a nonzero cover, so every $B$-simple/projective orbit arises this way. Distinct surviving heads remain distinct after quotienting because a $B$-isomorphism of the descended covers would give an $A$-isomorphism of the original covers after inflation, and distinct original heads stay distinct; hence the surviving projective-cover shift orbits cannot merge, and extension of scalars is surjective on projective $K_0$.

Dualities. For finite $P$, evaluation on shifted free modules and restriction to retracts identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes_AP,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_AB$, and applying the generator-fixing anti-involution $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes_AP)^\#=B\otimes_AP^\#$. Inflation does not change the finite vector duality $D_\psi$ of a simple, since the underlying vector space and the $\psi$-action are unchanged. The choice-free normalization clauses of [F2] therefore carry the unique $\#$-self-dual generic covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to unique normalized $B$-covers and simples.

The two pairings. For normalized labels, $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)=q^a$ in a single shift $a$ because $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ absolutely, while distinct heads give zero; assigning the simple's shift makes $h=\delta_{P,S}$. Similarly $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)=\delta_{P,S}$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ for evaluation of a tensor functional; $T$ is bilinear in the two arguments and $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ is first-bar sesquilinear. Extension of scalars induces the surjection on projective $K_0$ by step 2.1. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal statement is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

**Ungraded monic deformations.** For a general monic
specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

**Status of further structure.** Exactness, preservation of projectives and a
shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is

and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. derivations.claim: The vacuum is a nonzero highest-weight vector. The rank-zero block is $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, so $1_\Lambda=[k]$ is nonzero; restriction from root zero has zero target, so $E_i1_\Lambda=0$ for every $i$; and the torus acts on the root-zero component by $q^{\langle a,\Lambda\rangle}$, so its weight is $\Lambda$.

Divided generation. The quotient-cover lemma [F3] makes extension of scalars surjective on split $K_0$, so it suffices to generate the generic $K_0$ by extensions of divided words. The generic negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$ and its divided-power projectives with the divided generators; their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors applied to the vacuum, so the classes $F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over $A$. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient, which is exactly why the stronger generation statement must use divided words. torus acts on root component $\beta$ by
$K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed
relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to
$\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This
does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$
submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.

For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

derivations.claim: The two normalizations agree with the actions. The normalized-action supplier [F1] gives, for $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$, the exponent $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization; the same computation with the factor on $F$ gives the Kang--Kashiwara normalization. Both satisfy the mixed relations, the full Serre families and local nilpotence, and $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$ in all cases; hence all four displayed operator families are integrable weight module structures after scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$, with no assertion of finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules in affine or indefinite type.

Bilinearity and perfectness of $T$. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, so $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma [F2] gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness in normalized bases; shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same power of $q$, which is exactly $A$-bilinearity. Finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, so $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$, which is first-bar-sesquilinear rather than bilinear.

Adjointness of the two normalized actions. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity of the balanced tensor over the corner gives $T_B(F^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)=T_A(P,E^{\mathrm{basic}}M)$: both sides are the dimension of the same balanced tensor. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,F^{\mathrm{basic}}M)=T_A(E^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)$ as well, the corner factors becoming $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order with multiplication giving the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement, and the first identity gives the other; neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem is used.

The defect rescaling. Adding an $i$ changes the defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$, so the two module actions of step 1.1 are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ with $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$; the same computation applies on projective $K_0$ with the roles of $E$ and $F$ exchanged. Hence the canonical and Kang--Kashiwara normalizations define the same quantum structure up to the stated conjugation, completing the proof.

By [F1], $1_\Lambda$ is nonzero, has weight $\Lambda$ and is killed by every $E_i$; by [F2] the operators satisfy the full quantum relations and are locally nilpotent, so the $A$-submodule $U_A^-1_\Lambda\subseteq K_0(R^\Lambda)$ is a highest-weight module generated by a highest vector of weight $\Lambda$, and [F1] says it is all of $K_0(R^\Lambda)$.

The universal map from $V_A(\Lambda)$. The universal property of the integral highest-weight module ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]], with the canonical highest vector of the simple quotient of [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]] and the integral form $V_A(\Lambda)=U_A^-v_\Lambda$ of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]) gives a surjective $A$-linear map $\varphi:V_A(\Lambda)\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$ sending the canonical highest vector to $1_\Lambda$ and the divided powers of the negative half to the divided-word classes; it is surjective by step 1.1. The generic negative-half categorification [F3] identifies the divided words with the divided-power projectives of the generic $K_0$, whose extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors; the divided powers are those of the divided-power integral form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), so $\varphi$ is $A$-linear on the divided bases and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism by the triangularity of the two divided bases.

Compatibility with the pairing and the bases. The normalized action theorem [F2] gives the weightwise perfect tensor pairing in normalized projective-cover/simple bases, and the image of the canonical pairing of $V_A(\Lambda)$ under the identification of step 2.1 is the same form ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]], [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]) because both are determined by the values on the normalized generators; hence the identification is compatible with the perfect pairing and with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of indecomposable projectives. The construction uses the declared generic suppliers [F3] and inherits the Axiom of Choice only through the generic negative-half and integral highest-weight contracts, no other step using infinite choice.
