Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and any
real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, let
$K_0(R^\Lambda)$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective
$R^\Lambda$-modules with its $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module structure and
Cartan map of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]].
Then the normalized functors of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
equip $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ with the structure of the integral highest-weight
$U_A(\mathfrak g)$-module $V_A(\Lambda)$ with highest vector
$1_\Lambda=[k]$, via the unique $A$-linear isomorphism sending the divided
words to the divided powers of the negative half acting on the highest vector.
The identification is compatible with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of
indecomposable projectives and with the perfect tensor pairing.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

derivations.claim: Perfectness and the dual isomorphism. By [F1] each weight component has finitely many absolutely simple graded shift orbits and normalized projective covers, and the exactness of projective tensor pairing together with the unscaled diagonal values gives perfectness over $A$ on each weight. Hence $G_0$ is free on the simple classes and the functional map $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$ is an isomorphism from $G_0(R^\Lambda)$ to the weightwise dual $\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A)$, i.e. the restricted weight dual and not a full unrestricted product dual.

Intertwining with the canonical action. Transport $K_0$ by $\phi$; its tensor form is the actual highest-weight contravariant form with $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$ ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]). From tensor adjunction, $T(P,F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}M)=T(E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)=T(\sigma(F_i)P,M)$, and the analogous normalized identity is $T(P,E_i^{\mathrm{can}}M)=T(\sigma(E_i)P,M)$; these are precisely the restricted contravariant-dual action relations, so $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ intertwines the canonical module action with the dual action and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis.

The KK normalization and the Hom pairing. The Kang--Kashiwara action differs from the canonical one by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ on root $\beta$, so its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$; in particular the unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ by [F1] and is first-bar-sesquilinear, which concerns the other duality and does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification. The Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the integral projective identification [F2] and the contravariant-form suppliers [F3].

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up
to internal shift. Set $c_i(S)=\epsilon_i^L(S)$ and
$J_i(S)=\max\{n\ge0:c_i(f_i^nS)=c_i(S)\}$. This maximum is finite and
$J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for
$\beta=\operatorname{wt}(S)$. For $i\ne j$ one has $c_i(f_jS)=c_i(S)$; for
$j=i$ it stays constant or increases by $1$, and increase is equivalent to
$f_iS=f_i^LS$ and to simplicity of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L(i))$. Once it
increases, it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Put
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,
\operatorname{wt}\rangle$. The maps
$\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ are strict injective
elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at
some $i$. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic $f_i$
nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$ the actual
surviving lowering length is
$\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. All containing-weight
arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum,
leaving $R,A,D,Q$ unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the
original $P$ is added. Linear divided restriction/$G_0$ operators satisfy the
quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to
satisfy a linear Serre identity.

For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal
has strict elementary embeddings
$\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c_i(b))$, where $c_i(b)=\epsilon_i(*b)$,
$\bar b=(e_i^*)^{c_i(b)}b$, $c_i(\bar b)=0$, and every nonvacuum vertex has
positive extraction for some $i$. The negative-half reversal $*$ permutes
$B(\infty)$ without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing
signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not
assumed. The survivors of $\pi_\lambda$ are exactly $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for
all $i$; with weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$, inherited raising and
surviving lowering, and $\epsilon/\varphi$, they are $B(\lambda)$. Any two
lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict
nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum
vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite
color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field
and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ of the first two lemmas, the
shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically $B(\infty)$, its first-strand
cyclotomic simple graph is $B(\lambda)$, and the graph labeled by
indecomposable projective COVERS $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled
cover--simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators
transported on cover labels; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification,
generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the
projective class is used.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and any
real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, let
$K_0(R^\Lambda)$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective
$R^\Lambda$-modules with its $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module structure and
Cartan map of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]].
Then the normalized functors of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
equip $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ with the structure of the integral highest-weight
$U_A(\mathfrak g)$-module $V_A(\Lambda)$ with highest vector
$1_\Lambda=[k]$, via the unique $A$-linear isomorphism sending the divided
words to the divided powers of the negative half acting on the highest vector.
The identification is compatible with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of
indecomposable projectives and with the perfect tensor pairing.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

derivations.claim: The simple graph. Inflate a cyclotomic simple to the generic algebra; by [F1] the one-step restriction has a single simple socle and head once and induction has the unique simple head, giving well-defined operators $\widetilde e_i,\widetilde f_i$ on shift orbits with $\varepsilon_i$ decreasing by one under $\widetilde e_i$ and increasing by one under $\widetilde f_i$. By [F2] the graph is lowering-generated with strict elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex, over every field including positive characteristic.

Identification with $B(\Lambda)$. Apply the canonical elementary extraction of [F3]: the generic simple graph is canonically $B(\infty)$ and the first-strand cyclotomic survivors are exactly the vertices with $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$, which is the crystal $B(\Lambda)$ with vacuum $u_\Lambda$; the survivor criterion is $\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{LEFT}}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$ by the first-dot index of [F1]. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, so no quantum-factorial multiplicity enters.

Projective labels. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers: the quotient-cover lemma pairs each projective cover with its simple head without scaling and preserves the label under the quotient, while the two Grothendieck identifications of [F3] record the same labels on $K_0$ and $G_0$. The projective graph is therefore explicitly transported from the simple labels, not obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the canonical extraction and crystal-existence suppliers of [F3].

citations.quote: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every $i$, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $Af$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free $A$-rank of $Af_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.

On the generic graded KLR algebra define $\rho(e(\nu))=e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$,
$\rho(x_a)=x_{n+1-a}$, $\rho(\tau_a)=-\tau_{n-a}$. This is a degree-preserving
ALGEBRA AUTOMORPHISM with $\rho^2=1$, commuting with the generator-fixing
anti-involution $\psi$. It maps $e(\nu)Re(\eta)$ to
$e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)Re(\operatorname{rev}\eta)$. Twisting LEFT modules by
$a\cdot m=\rho(a)m$ is an equivalence and commutes with finite vector duality
and projective Hom duality. Its separated-block formula is
$\rho^*\operatorname{Ind}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Ind}(\rho^*N,\rho^*M)$,
without a shift. Under $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ it induces the quantum
multiplication-reversing star, fixing every $F_i$ and $q$. The first
cyclotomic generator maps to $a_{\nu_1}(x_n)e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$, with the
SAME original first color. Thus it identifies the first- and last-strand
quotients; preservation of the first ideal itself is not asserted in general.

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal
has strict elementary embeddings
$\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c_i(b))$, where $c_i(b)=\epsilon_i(*b)$,
$\bar b=(e_i^*)^{c_i(b)}b$, $c_i(\bar b)=0$, and every nonvacuum vertex has
positive extraction for some $i$. The negative-half reversal $*$ permutes
$B(\infty)$ without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing
signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not
assumed. The survivors of $\pi_\lambda$ are exactly $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for
all $i$; with weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$, inherited raising and
surviving lowering, and $\epsilon/\varphi$, they are $B(\lambda)$. Any two
lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict
nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum
vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite
color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field
and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ of the first two lemmas, the
shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically $B(\infty)$, its first-strand
cyclotomic simple graph is $B(\lambda)$, and the graph labeled by
indecomposable projective COVERS $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled
cover--simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators
transported on cover labels; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification,
generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the
projective class is used.

For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient over any field with the
general real symmetrizable datum and graded KLR parameters, let
$\mathcal B_\Lambda$ be the normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes. Set
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=\Lambda-\beta$,
$\varepsilon_i(S)=\max\{r:(E_i^{\mathrm{basic}})^rS\ne0\}$ and
$\varphi_i(S)=\varepsilon_i(S)+\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}(S)\rangle$. For
$\varepsilon_i>0$, define $\widetilde e_iS$ by the unique simple isomorphism
type in the socle of one-step right restriction, with its unique self-dual
normalization; define $\widetilde f_iS$ by the simple head of right induction
when nonzero, otherwise zero. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, not
a quantum-factorial multiplicity. These data form a crystal canonically
isomorphic to $B(\Lambda)$, with vacuum sent to $u_\Lambda$. The normalized
indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple
heads and covers. The projective graph here is explicitly transported from
these labels, rather than obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an
unspecified projective basis. The highest-weight quotient has simple survivors
exactly when $\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{LEFT}}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$.

For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and any
real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, let
$K_0(R^\Lambda)$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective
$R^\Lambda$-modules with its $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module structure and
Cartan map of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]].
Then the normalized functors of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
equip $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ with the structure of the integral highest-weight
$U_A(\mathfrak g)$-module $V_A(\Lambda)$ with highest vector
$1_\Lambda=[k]$, via the unique $A$-linear isomorphism sending the divided
words to the divided powers of the negative half acting on the highest vector.
The identification is compatible with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of
indecomposable projectives and with the perfect tensor pairing.

derivations.claim: Survival and non-merging. For a surviving normalized generic simple $S$, quotient Hom base change in the cover-descent lemma [F3] sends its normalized projective cover to the cyclotomic normalized cover, commutes with $\#$, and preserves its unscaled head pairing; if its simple is killed, the quotient is zero, because any nonzero finite quotient of the cover has a simple head and adjunction would produce a surviving generic head of the original cover. Thus raw extension of a generic normalized indecomposable projective is zero or a single normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective, and distinct surviving heads do not merge; the image is $\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$ respectively $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$ under the projections of [F1].

RIGHT-simple labels. In RIGHT-simple labels $c$, the generic FIRST-recursion theorem gives $\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$, so raw extension sends the class to $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$, which is exactly the crystal-compatible survivor label produced by [F3]. Every normalized cyclotomic cover is obtained because every cyclotomic simple inflates to a generic simple whose cover descends. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and quantum-projection contracts of [F1] and the canonical-extraction supplier of [F3]; no other step uses infinite choice. The claim concerns indecomposable projectives, not every finite projective quotient.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ be a standard graded cyclotomic block
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]) and let $\psi$ be the
descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$; it is well defined
because its individual first-strand polynomial generators are fixed, and it is
the generator-fixing member of the two $\psi$'s in play
([[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]). Write shifts internally as $(M\{r\})_m=
M_{m-r}$ ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]).

**Vector duality.** For a finite graded $B$-module $M$ define
$$D_\psi M:=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi,$$
the finite $k$-linear dual with $B$-action $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. It is a
finite graded $B$-module, reverses internal shifts, and $D_\psi^2M\cong M$.

**Projective Hom duality.** For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead
$$P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi,$$
with the $\psi$-twisted $B$-action. This is again a finite graded projective,
it reverses internal shifts, and $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ on finite graded
projectives ([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]).

**They are different dualities.** Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective
simple to produce its cover; $D_\psi$ and $\#$ differ already in rank one,
where $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ has $B^\#=B$ while $D_\psi B\cong B\{-2d_i
(\lambda-1)\}$.

**Normalizations used in the based statements.** By
[[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]],
each simple shift orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and
its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is
$\#$-self-dual; these normalized representatives are the ones used in the based
statements below. The symmetric theorem
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]
additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$;
it does not change the canonical projective normalization. No self-dual shift
is asserted for every indecomposable finite module, and no choice is used.

derivations.claim: Cover classes land on lower global vectors. By [F1] all normalized cyclotomic covers are precisely the nonzero extensions of normalized generic covers, with distinct surviving simple heads; the based-quotient lemma sends each such class to a single positive lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, with no grading ambiguity because Hom base change preserves the $\#$-normalization and the degree-zero head pairing.

Surjectivity. Conversely the quantum global projection theorem [F2] supplies a generic global vector lifting every lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, and the generic theorem supplies its normalized generic cover; mirroring if necessary to use the raw first/right convention, its extension has that nonzero class and is a normalized indecomposable cover. Hence the assignment is surjective onto the lower basis.

Bijectivity and labels. The integral $K_0$ isomorphism and its free normalized projective basis make the assignment injective; the RIGHT crystal label identification of [F3] shows that the projective with RIGHT label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to $G^-_\Lambda(c)$, with the FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism classes, not of generic lifts, and no arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and projection contracts of [F2].

real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, let

Cartan map of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]].

[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]

$U_A(\mathfrak g)$-module $V_A(\Lambda)$ with highest vector
$1_\Lambda=[k]$, via the unique $A$-linear isomorphism sending the divided
words to the divided powers of the negative half acting on the highest vector.
The identification is compatible with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of
indecomposable projectives and with the perfect tensor pairing.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$

CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}

asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$

**Vector duality.** For a finite graded $B$-module $M$ define

$$P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi,$$

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and
admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block
$B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and
$R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put
$\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero
block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional
$\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree
$t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is
vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded
bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with
$P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has
$D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives.
This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality
of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation
polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric
UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and
homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is
the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree
$-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

derivations.claim: Projective Hom self-duality. Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)^\psi\cong B=P$ directly, the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module; hence the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift.

Vector duality and the shift. The functional $\epsilon(x^a)=0$ for $a<\lambda-1$ and $\epsilon(x^{\lambda-1})=1$ is the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace; it has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its anti-diagonal pairing $\epsilon(x^ax^b)=\delta_{a+b,\lambda-1}$ is perfect over every field, so $D_\psi B\cong B\{-2(\lambda-1)\}$. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality of $P\{s\}$ solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$, while projective Hom self-duality solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$.

The general defect shift and the boundary. For a general normalized cyclotomic projective the same computation with the symmetric theorem gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$, which is a comparison of the two dualities and does not redefine the projective normalization. At $\lambda=1$ the two centers agree; at $\lambda=2$ they differ by $1$ as computed; at $\lambda=0$ the defining relation is $1=0$ and the block vanishes, so there is no indecomposable projective here. The trace is never halved to pick the lower-basis class.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

derivations.claim: The word class. By [F1] the word projective decomposes as $(q+q^{-1})$ copies of $P_{i,2}$, so $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}]$; under the K_0 isomorphism of the integral projective theorem this is the class of the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$.

The divided power and the scalar. By [F2], $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}=[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$ with $[2]_{q_i}=q+q^{-1}$, and the lower global basis vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$; the scalar $q+q^{-1}$ is not of the form $\pm q^n$, so rescaling by it is not a unit change of $A$-basis and the word class cannot be the global basis element in that weight.

Conclusion. No purely K_0-theoretic identification can produce the divided power without dividing by $[2]_{q_i}$; the missing input is exactly the self-dual shift normalization and the positivity of the extension-of-scalars theorem, which are additional structures on top of the bare isomorphism $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$. This refutes the stated claim, and the rank-two comparison is a finite computation using no choice.

Take $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$ and
$\Lambda=\lambda\Lambda_1$ with $\lambda\ge0$, so that the standard cyclotomic
quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] imposes
$x_1^{\lambda}e(\nu)=0$ on every word. Then:

(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$; for $1\le n\le\lambda$,
$R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^{\lambda})$ with graded dimension
$\sum_{r<\lambda}\dim(\mathrm{Pol}_n)_r\,q^{2r}$ in the nil-Hecke presentation,
and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n>\lambda$;

(b) at $\lambda=1$ and $n=1$ the block is $k$ with $x_1=0$ and there is no
nonzero simple projective at root $\alpha_i$ in the higher-quotient sense,
while at $\lambda\ge1$ the rank-one block $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^\lambda$
has graded dimension $1+q^2+\cdots+q^{2(\lambda-1)}$ and its regular module
decomposes as $[\lambda]_q$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective
$P_{i,1}$ only when the normalization is fixed as in
[[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; in particular
$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=0$ for $\lambda=1$, and for $\lambda=2$ one has
$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus(q+q^{-1})}$;

(c) the inhomogeneous monic deformation $a_i(u)=u(u-1)$ at $\lambda=2$ gives
$R^\Lambda_a(\alpha_i)=k\oplus k$ rather than $k[x]/x^2$: its two ordinary
simple projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of
$V(2)$, so the standard graded hypothesis is substantive.

Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the
composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping
fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}.$$

Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an
isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real
symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and
$q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; on module $G_0$ use
either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization
$E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$,
$F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$. In all cases
$K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed
and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to
$\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or
indefinite type.

The tensor pairing
$T_\beta(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is
$A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple
bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$
instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$,
projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$ and projective $F_i$
to module $E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the
weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where
$\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.

derivations.claim: The blocks. By [F1] the nonzero blocks are $k$ at roots $0,\alpha_i$ (with $x_1=0$ at root $\alpha_i$ for the first block) and $0$ at $2\alpha_i$ and beyond, so the only nontrivial functor values on the vacuum are $F^\Lambda_ik=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_ik=0$.

The commutator. The relation of [F2] evaluated on the vacuum gives $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_ik\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ by [F1], so $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ holds at the first nontrivial weight.

The Grothendieck commutator. With the normalizations of [F3]: projective $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=q^{-1}(1+q^2)[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$; KK module $F$ from the vacuum also carries $q^{-1}$ while KK $E$ is raw, and the canonical module action shifts $E$ and leaves $F$ raw, giving the same result in both module conventions. All agree with $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})$, the mixed relation evaluated at $K_i=q^2$. This verifies the commutator identity at the first nontrivial weight and is a finite rank-one computation using no choice.

Take $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$ and
$\Lambda=\lambda\Lambda_1$ with $\lambda\ge0$, so that the standard cyclotomic
quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] imposes

(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$; for $1\le n\le\lambda$,
$R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^{\lambda})$ with graded dimension
$\sum_{r<\lambda}\dim(\mathrm{Pol}_n)_r\,q^{2r}$ in the nil-Hecke presentation,
and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n>\lambda$;

(b) at $\lambda=1$ and $n=1$ the block is $k$ with $x_1=0$ and there is no
nonzero simple projective at root $\alpha_i$ in the higher-quotient sense,
while at $\lambda\ge1$ the rank-one block $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^\lambda$
has graded dimension $1+q^2+\cdots+q^{2(\lambda-1)}$ and its regular module
decomposes as $[\lambda]_q$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective
$P_{i,1}$ only when the normalization is fixed as in
[[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; in particular
$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=0$ for $\lambda=1$, and for $\lambda=2$ one has
$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus(q+q^{-1})}$;

(c) the inhomogeneous monic deformation $a_i(u)=u(u-1)$ at $\lambda=2$ gives
$R^\Lambda_a(\alpha_i)=k\oplus k$ rather than $k[x]/x^2$: its two ordinary
simple projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of
$V(2)$, so the standard graded hypothesis is substantive.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and any
real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, let
$K_0(R^\Lambda)$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective
$R^\Lambda$-modules with its $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module structure and
Cartan map of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]].
Then the normalized functors of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
equip $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ with the structure of the integral highest-weight
$U_A(\mathfrak g)$-module $V_A(\Lambda)$ with highest vector
$1_\Lambda=[k]$, via the unique $A$-linear isomorphism sending the divided
words to the divided powers of the negative half acting on the highest vector.
The identification is compatible with the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-bases of
indecomposable projectives and with the perfect tensor pairing.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

derivations.claim: The blocks and their composition structure. By [F1] the three nonzero blocks have dimensions $1$, $2$ and $q+q^{-1}$; the first regular module $B_1$ has two composition factors $S_1,S_1\{2\}$ with graded dimensions $1+q^2$, and the second block is the endomorphism matrix algebra of the graded column $S_2$, whose regular left module is the column tensored with its graded vector dual of dimension $q+q^{-1}$.

The Cartan pairing. The normalized cover-to-head Hom space is $k$ in degree zero and there are no other simple types in a block, so quotient-cover evaluation of [F2] identifies the tensor pairing with $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with distinct roots paired by zero. The integral identification of [F3] maps $P_0,P_1,P_2$ to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ to $F^2v$, and in $G_0$ the regular classes are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$.

The restricted dual. The canonical restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided lower vector, and since $T$ pairs $P_r$ with $S_s$ by $\delta_{rs}$ it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$; the scalar $q+q^{-1}$ is not removed by the pairing. This is a cover/simple pairing computation, not a claim that the Cartan matrix is all ones or that a trace removes a denominator, and it is a finite computation using no choice.
